issues.description: Method mismatch for SealSaloon.checkOrderReady(): The problem statement (UML and text) declares checkOrderReady() as void (no return value), while the reference implementation in the solution repository defines the method as returning boolean (public boolean checkOrderReady()). This inconsistency affects the method signature students are expected to implement and may confuse them about whether a return value is part of the contract and what its meaning should be.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the expected signature consistent between the specification and the reference implementation. Two options:
1) If the intended behavior is to return whether any order was served, update the problem statement (UML and textual description) to declare checkOrderReady(): boolean and document the meaning of the boolean return value (e.g., true when at least one order was served). Also update any tests or examples to reflect the boolean return.
2) If the intended contract is a void method (as currently in the problem statement), modify the reference solution so checkOrderReady() is declared void and remove the boolean return value (preserve the internal logic but do not return any value). Update any callers/tests to use the void signature.
Choose one option and apply it consistently to the problem statement, template, solution, and tests so students have a single, unambiguous method signature to follow.
